---
title: "Start here"
description: "Install rpgeom, compute a budget, and audit a matrix."
---

## Install

```bash
git clone https://github.com/piyush314/random-projection-geometry.git
cd random-projection-geometry
python -m pip install -e ".[dev]"
pytest -q
```

The package requires Python 3.10+ and runs on CPU. Until the public PyPI
release, an editable Git checkout is the canonical installation.

## 1. Ask what a sketch can retain

```bash
rpgeom budget --d 768 --m 64 --q 10
rpgeom budget --d 768 --m 64 --q 10 --json
```

`hgr_ceiling` is a correlation ceiling, while `shape_ratio` and `mean_ratio`
are information fractions. The report labels these different units explicitly.

## 2. Choose a dimension from a target

```bash
rpgeom recommend --d 768 --kendall-tau 0.30
rpgeom recommend --d 768 --q 10 --nearest-neighbor 0.35
```

The returned `m` is the smallest integer satisfying every supplied target under
the stated Gaussian model. Treat it as a principled baseline, then audit data.

## 3. Audit your matrix

```bash
rpgeom audit embeddings.npy --m 64 --q 10 --trials 5000 --seed 7 --json
```

Rows are observations and columns are features. The audit centers the matrix,
reports its spectral trace ratio and leading-eigenspace recovery share, draws a
seeded Haar subspace, and measures comparison and neighbor survival.
